shots.title: HOW A 747 WING ACTUALLY LIFTS
shots.purpose: Put the carrying problem on screen first: the wing holding 400 tonnes
shots.claim: a loaded 747 can weigh up to 400 tonnes
shots.evidence: full-bleed underside plate of a 747 wing with engines, weight figure popped as annotation
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the blueprint slice when the engineering starts

subject_contract.expected_subject: underside view of a large four-engine airliner wing drawn in vintage ink-wash style
required: swept aircraft wing seen from below

one_second.relationship: the wing itself is the subject carrying the weight

shots.purpose: Introduce the engineer's view: a wing reduced to one cross-section
shots.claim: lift comes from the wing's cross-sectional shape
shots.evidence: blueprint card: edge-on airfoil slice on a grid with chord line and camber curve labelled
shots.motion_reason: near-static drift so the annotation is the motion, not the camera
shots.transition_reason: hard cut into the reveal card of the same airfoil

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment blueprint card of a single airfoil cross-section with chord line

one_second.relationship: a wing is one curved slice repeated across the span

shots.purpose: Reveal the airfoil geometry itself: curved top, flatter bottom
shots.claim: the airfoil has a curved upper surface and a flat trailing section
shots.evidence: airfoil card with streamlines bending over the camber and a highlight on the curve
shots.motion_reason: push toward the upper surface while streamlines carry the story
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the pressure map of the same section

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of an airfoil cross-section with flowing streamline curves above it
required: streamline lines flowing left to right

one_second.relationship: streamlines squeeze over the curved top surface

shots.purpose: Show the pressure field: suction above, pressure below
shots.claim: pressure above the wing is lower than pressure below it
shots.evidence: split pressure card with sparse suction arrows above and dense push arrows below
shots.motion_reason: hold the comparison still; the arrow density is the information
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the streamtube explanation

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram comparing sparse long arrows above an airfoil with dense short arrows below

one_second.relationship: low pressure above, high pressure below

shots.purpose: Explain the mechanism: a squeezed streamtube speeds up and loses pressure
shots.claim: faster flow over the curved top means lower pressure above the wing
shots.evidence: streamtube card with narrow fast section over the camber and wide slow section beneath
shots.motion_reason: drift along the tube so the narrowing reads as acceleration
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the macro streamline detail

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of a flow tube narrowing over an airfoil curve with speed arrows

one_second.relationship: narrow tube: faster air, lower pressure

shots.purpose: Rest the eye inside the flow itself: ink-wash streamlines over camber
shots.claim: the flow follows the curved surface before recovering behind the wing
shots.evidence: tight macro of engraved streamlines hugging the curved surface
shots.motion_reason: slow zoom reveals the surface following the curves
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the Newton card

subject_contract.expected_subject: engraved close-up of parallel streamline curves bending over a cambered surface

one_second.relationship: air hugging the curve of the surface

shots.purpose: Complete the physics: downwash behind the wing, reaction up
shots.claim: the wing deflects air downward and the reaction pushes the wing up
shots.evidence: Newton card: airfoil deflecting streamlines downward with a large rust reaction arrow up
shots.motion_reason: the arrow pair is the animation: downwash down, reaction up
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the stall card

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of an airfoil deflecting airflow downward with one large upward arrow
required: airfoil at a small nose-up angle

one_second.relationship: air pushed down, wing pushed up

shots.purpose: Twist: the same curve stops working when pushed too far
shots.claim: past a critical nose-up angle the flow separates and lift collapses
shots.evidence: before/after card: attached flow at small angle, separated tumble at large angle
shots.motion_reason: the transformation from attached to separated flow is the motion
shots.transition_reason: hard cut back to the dusk wing for the payoff

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment before-and-after card of attached airflow versus separated swirling airflow on an airfoil

one_second.relationship: attached flow lifts; separated flow does not

shots.purpose: Land the argument on the same wing, now carrying its explanation
shots.claim: in cruise, lift balances the aircraft's 400-tonne weight
shots.evidence: dusk underside wing plate reprising the opening composition
shots.motion_reason: slow pull to rest; the strongest composition holds still

subject_contract.expected_subject: underside view of an airliner wing at dusk drawn in vintage ink-wash style

one_second.relationship: the wing at dusk, still holding the weight
